title: Adapt the Object to the Subject: Representative Study Material for Empirical Software Engineering
abstract: arXiv:2611.07772v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: External validity is a central concern in empirical software engineering, yet the debate has largely focused on whether study participants are representative. How well the study objects they reason about - code, models, or requirements - are representative of each participant's own work is often overlooked. Practitioners' own artifacts would be ideal, but are often out of reach, so researchers sample from public datasets or construct objects artificially. Whether this lack of subject-object fit affects participants' ability to act on the material remains unknown. We take a first step toward answering this question for requirements. We propose an approach that uses an LLM to generate context-adapted synthetic requirements just-in-time during an online survey from a short, participant-supplied context description, optionally injecting requirements smells as controlled stimuli. To validate the approach, we conducted a controlled experiment

translated_title: 让客体适应主体：面向实证软件工程的代表性研究材料
translated_abstract: 外部效度是实证软件工程中的核心关注点，然而相关讨论大多聚焦于研究参与者是否具有代表性，而参与者所面对的研究对象——代码、模型或需求——在多大程度上能代表每位参与者自己的实际工作，却常常被忽视。从业者自身的工件（artifact）虽然是最理想的材料，但往往难以获取，因此研究人员通常从公开数据集中抽样或人工构造研究对象。这种主体与客体之间的不匹配是否会影响参与者对材料进行处理的能力，目前尚不清楚。我们朝着回答这一问题（针对需求领域）迈出了第一步。我们提出了一种方法：利用大语言模型（LLM）在在线调查过程中，根据参与者提供的简短上下文描述即时（just-in-time）生成适配上下文的合成需求，并可选择性地注入需求坏味（requirements smells）作为受控刺激。为验证该方法，我们进行了一项受控实验……
tldr: 该论文首次关注实证软件工程中“研究对象与被试自身工作不匹配”这一被忽视的外部效度问题，并提出一种利用LLM在在线调查中根据参与者简短上下文描述即时生成适配语境的合成需求（可注入需求坏味作为受控刺激）的实验方法。
en_tdlr: The paper addresses the overlooked external validity issue of subject-object fit in empirical software engineering by proposing an LLM-based approach that generates context-adapted synthetic requirements just-in-time during online surveys from short participant-supplied context descriptions, with optional requirements smells as controlled stimuli.
